To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the modified DIS is a more reliable measure of current symptoms than the unmodified DIS and that the unmodified version of the DIS overestimates 1-month period prevalences for Major Depressive Episodes.

the modified DIS provides more accurate information on the current state of mental disorders than the unmodified DIS and that the unmodified version overestimates the 1-month prevalence rate for Major Depressive Episodes.

(a) the modified DIS provides a better estimate of current mental status than the unmodified DIS; (b) the modified DIS is a better measure of current symptomatology than a count of the number of symptoms reported on the unmodified DIS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability and validity of the NIMH diagnostic interviews.
the development and evaluation of the DIS as a research and clinical instrument.
the development and evaluation of a diagnostic instrument for use in large-scale epidemiological surveys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unmodified NIMH Diagnostic Interview Schedule may overestimate the prevalence of major depressive disorder, but not necessarily other disorders, in community surveys.
the modified DIS is a more valid measure of current mental status than the unmodified DIS.
the modified DIS provides a more accurate measure of current mental status than does the unmodified DIS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified DIS is a valuable tool for field surveys of current mental health status, but that the unmodified version is not.
the modified DIS is a more reliable and valid instrument for assessing current mental status than the unmodified DIS.
the unmodified NIMH-DIS is not suitable for use in surveys of mental disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modified DIS provides more accurate estimates of 1-month period prevalences for Major Depressive Disorder and for the other disorders that we studied, including the 12-month prevalence estimates.

the modified DIS is a useful instrument for obtaining information on current mental disorders and symptoms, and for distinguishing persons who meet all diagnostic criteria for a disorder at or around interview from former cases.
the unmodified version of the DIS is not a reliable instrument to assess current symptom status in field surveys.
